attributes.residual: THE MECHANISM, and a calibration note on two tools. The aligned view shows this is NOT a recolor at all: it is a two-instruction SWAP. Retail emits `@0x94 mtctr r0`, `@0x98 li r5,0`, `@0x9c addi r4,r3,0 @lbl_8025776C(ADDR16_LO)`; we emit `mtctr r0`, `addi r4,r3,0 @...(ADDR16_LO)`, `li r5,0`. The `fnasm --raw --diff` view pairs them with a target-only/ours-only pair (`<` and `>` rows), which is the correct reading, while `wf_word_diff` - which aligns by INDEX - calls the same thing 'CLASS: RECOLOR, only register fields differ' and the operand-provenance screen, screening index-aligned slots, calls it BASE-FORM-DIFF. Both are artifacts of index alignment across a displacement, and this pair is a good two-sided calibration case for either tool: a 2-word 'recolor' that is really a 2-instruction schedule swap. The residual class is SCHEDULE, the two instructions are mutually independent, and no statement-level lever reaches it - probe (2) shows the address materialisation moves readily but drags the surrounding colouring with it, six-fold.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Check whether the two swapped instructions really are independent - if `addi r4,r3,0` depended on r5, or `li r5,0` on r4, the order would be forced and no scheduler story applies. Read from the aligned view 2026-09-03: `li r5,0` writes r5 from nothing and `addi r4,r3,0 @lbl_8025776C(ADDR16_LO)` writes r4 from r3 (set at +0x90 `lis r3`), so they share no register and are genuinely independent. A cursor-loop rewrite that changes the instruction COUNT away from 104/108 also refutes the hypothesis immediately, since the count parity is currently exact and must be preserved.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - both windows, the `lis r3` definition site feeding the addi, and the independence of the two swapped instructions were read from `fnasm.py ... --raw --diff` against the retail bytes.
hypothesis.statement: The two swapped instructions are independent, so the order is a scheduler decision on the loop preheader, not a source-order one - which is why moving the source statements either did nothing (probe 1) or moved everything (probe 2). The untried axis is the one that changes the preheader's CONTENTS rather than its order: the `mtctr r0` immediately above is the loop-count setup for a bdnz that MWCC synthesised from `i < 32, i += 4`, and a loop written with an explicit pointer cursor instead of a scaled integer index (`for (p = tbl; p < tbl + 32; p += 4)`) produces a different preheader with one fewer live value, which is the only structural change available at 104 instructions.
